children: A blank on a map can mean many things. We give each gap a type and a count, so a reader knows which kind of blank they are looking at.
The field does not exist anywhere we looked, such as a tax class.
The field exists but is mostly empty: property codes on 1,628 of 81,121 rows.
Old property codes that disagree with current zoning.
Values that stand in for nothing, such as roll numbers of all zeros on 10 parcels.
A postal code column blank on every row.
Some source data carries personal information about property holders. It exists, and we keep it from public view. No values are shown.
About 46 percent of City parcels, 74,276 of 166,745, sit outside the area where roll numbers are published.

"No data" is not one thing. A parcel outside a watershed and a field withheld for privacy both show a blank, for different reasons. The ledger keeps the reason, the count and the source, and the map can show the right words.
Each gap has a closing rule. A new source, a re-pull or an answer from the publisher can close it, and nothing closes on its own.
